dispatched_notes: 11 from the 1st Air Division table reproduced in the 303rd BG mission 078 report (91-04). Lost = 1 (42-5714, MACR 899): the only 91st BG aircraft among the 74 aircraft that b17flyingfortress.de tags with this status date (91-01 database query) besides 42-29741 (damaged). Treat as PROBABLE until checked against the 91st BG's own records (91stbombgroup.com is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read).

aircraft.loss_details: Enemy fighters knocked out engines #3 and #4 (91-01; the MACR text quoted there also says No. 4 feathered and No. 1 smoking). Seen at 1530 hrs from 20,000 ft at 48°40'N 06°40'E descending under control, four parachutes seen (observer 2nd Lt. Joseph A. Sulli). Crash-landed on a rail line south of Metz, France; salvaged by the Luftwaffe and used by KG 200 for spares.
aircraft.notes: Nickname given as 'Old Faithful II' (91-01 title) and 'Old Faithful' (91-02, IWM). Ex-306th BG 423rd BS (RD-S), to 91st BG 323rd BS 11 Sep 1943; 91-01/91-02 also list 322nd BS code LL-S (conflicting / other period). Squadron code+letter OR-N is from 91-01, not confirmed for this date. Crew names in 91-01 are informal (Bob, Joe, Art...). MACR 899 itself not consulted.

crew.name: Robert M. Slane
crew.note: Given as 'Bob Slane' in 91-01/91-02. Full name 'Robert M. Slane' (91st BG, POW Stalag Luft 3) from 91-05 NARA-derived POW listing; match by name and group only. Pilot role inferred from being listed first and the aircraft being lost 'with Bob Slane' (91-02). 91-02 note says the Slane crew were from the 401st BS. Rank not documented here.

crew.name: Joseph A. Johnson
crew.note: 'Joe Johnson' in 91-01; full name, rank and POW from IWM person record (91-03).

crew.name: Arthur G. Foster
crew.note: 'Art Foster' in 91-01, which says he returned to UK 19/9/44; IWM (91-03) gives evaded.

crew.name: Bill Runner
crew.note: Informal name only, as given in 91-01; full name not found.

crew.name: Sherman Sly
crew.note: As given in 91-01 (flight engineer/top turret); full name/rank not found.

crew.name: Charles J. Croth
crew.note: 'Chas Croth' in 91-01. Rank is the highest rank recorded by IWM, not necessarily rank on the date.

crew.name: Claud Smith
crew.note: As given in 91-01/91-02; full name, rank and burial not confirmed (a search for an ABMC/Fields of Honor record found none under 'Claud').

aircraft.loss_details: Battle damaged over Schweinfurt; pilot Lt Christensen wounded and died the next day. Co-pilot Lt Mendelsohn flew it back and crash-landed at RAF Tangmere, striking a tree. Not struck off: after a long repair it returned to service with the 401st BS (LL-D) (91-01, 91-02).
aircraft.notes: Crash-landed in the UK, long repair (not written off). Letters given only as 'DF-F/D/P' (91-01), so the aircraft letter on this date is unknown. Whether it bombed the target is not documented (the IWM Christensen narrative describes an abort - conflict).

crew.name: Harold Robert Christensen
crew.note: Wounded in the left arm, died the next day / after the crash-landing at Tangmere (died of wounds; 'KIA' used as closest schema value). IWM record (91-03) gives service numbers 17065567 (enlisted) / O-738094 and DSC, AM, PH, but its narrative says 'mission to Merseburg' and describes an abort with a non-feathering engine, flying home alone; that conflicts with the Schweinfurt attribution in the same archive's aircraft record. Recorded as found.

crew.name: Stuart Bernard Mendelsohn
crew.note: Flew the aircraft back and crash-landed at RAF Tangmere after Christensen was incapacitated (91-01, 91-03). Rank as on IWM record. Later KIA 31 Dec 1943 in 42-29895 'The Black Swan' (MACR 1975).

crew.name: Kenneth C. Homuth
crew.note: Named in the IWM Christensen narrative as the navigator who treated Christensen in the nose; Homuth's own record does not mention the date.

crew.name: Homer Edwin Chatfield
crew.note: IWM record says he treated wounded ball gunner S/Sgt Walter J. Molzon during a running fight with Me 109s on the return from Schweinfurt aboard 42-29741. Service number shown on IWM is incomplete; not recorded.

crew.name: Walter J. Molzon
crew.note: Named as the wounded ball turret gunner in the IWM Chatfield record.

research_gaps: 91stbombgroup.com (the main source: daily mission/loading lists) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool and a Cloudflare 'Attention Required' challenge in the browser; it was not bypassed. Only 2 of 11 aircraft identified. A person with browser access to 91stbombgroup.com (Daily Journal / mission loading lists) could likely complete this group.
americanairmuseum.com returns HTTP 403; the IWM American archive mirror (americanarchive.iwm.org.uk) worked and was used for person records.

Nine 91st BG aircraft, pilots and crews unknown. Searched: web search for 91st/14 Oct 1943/Schweinfurt crews, b17flyingfortress.de REST API (all aircraft tagged with this date: only 42-5714 and 42-29741 are 91st), Wikipedia, libertyladybook.com, 100thbg.com Black Week page (100th only).

Slane crew: 5 of 10 full names via IWM; bombardier 'Bill Runner', engineer 'Sherman Sly', waist 'Bob Solomon', tail 'Claud Smith' are informal names only. Pilot full name 'Robert M. Slane' is a name+group match only. MACR 899 not consulted (would give full names, ranks, serial numbers).

42-29741 crew: only 5 names connected to the date; the IWM record also links radio operator T/Sgt Lloyd Derousse (37375849) to the aircraft/pilot but not to this date, so he is not listed. The Christensen record narrative ('Merseburg', abort) conflicts with Schweinfurt.
No formation positions found; the 91st flew in the 1st CBW (91-04 table) but its slot (lead/high/low) is ambiguous in the extracted table.
